newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Leap-year effect brakes headline Dutch GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: Leap-year effect brakes headline Dutch GDP growth.

text.p: A "leap-year effect" held back the headline rate of Dutch economic growth in the first quarter of 1997 to a year-on-year rate of 2.1 percent, the national statistics office said on Thursday.
But figures adjusted to eliminate the effect of the extra day in February 1996 showed that Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew at an underlying year-on-year rate of about 3.0 percent.
The statistics office noted that this was in line with the pace of Dutch GDP growth in the second half of 1996.
The Dutch economy has performed more strongly than some of the larger European economies over the last year, with buoyant consumer spending providing the main thrust.
Growth of consumer spending is generally expected to slow down in 1997, but an acceleration of exports is expected to keep the overall growth rate up to around three percent.
The statistics office said severe cold in the first quarter of 1996 had boosted production of natural gas for heating homes but had depressed the construction industry's output.
The first quarter of 1997 was fairly mild, with lower gas production and higher construction output.
In the year-on-year comparison between the first quarter of 1997 and the first quarter of 1996 these factors more or less cancelled each other out.
